title: Screen P112 tetrad coefficient fusion under relaxed rank ceilings
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This package binds the selected P112 tetrad basis change to the gauge44 centre cut. On each of fourteen blocks, `U K` has four zero rows. A hybrid reader keeps the old cut on those rows and uses the inverse-transpose map on the four updated rows; a separate correction preserves the dirty baseline. Exact rational checks give `H^T d + C^T d = S^T d` and `H^T U K = S^T K`. The full hybrid has 225 coefficients, its correction has 152, and its net increase is 201 incidences over the original 176-add cut.

The selected cut precedes canonical phase `B`. For its exact state map `x_B = M_B x`, the verifier transports each centre readout as `A_post = M_B^-T A` and checks `M_B^T A_post = A` over all ordinary roles. The original cut becomes a 448-coefficient post-`B` reader on output ports. The retimed hybrid/correction supports and relaxed incidence-only sensitivities are:

| Fused tetrads | Hybrid support | Dirty correction | Added incidences vs. original | Incidence-only complex κ ceiling |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 450 | 52 | 326 | 0.003212495586 |
| 5 | 454 | 76 | 354 | 0.007657155804 |
| 9 | 441 | 140 | 405 | 0.015679681607 |
| 14 | 437 | 215 | 476 | 0.024130777318 |

The original cut window after `A` and before `B` has a different frame profile: all 112 output roles and all eight active private centre accumulators are in frame 0, and the 176 source-bound cut ADDs use that same frame. A hybrid consumer kept at this pre-`B` boundary therefore needs no candidate frame joins for its added terms; its three-block incidence-only sensitivity remains `0.004947467105`. This is exact frame compatibility, not proof that the changed coefficients or separate dirty-baseline correction can be installed in the native schedule.

The selected native execution gives a frame-compatibility caveat at the post-`B` boundary: the 112 output roles occupy distinct rank-8 frames, and the eight centre roles occupy frames 415–422. Their joint rank is 9 and their only common selected frame is frame 1. None of the 448 original retimed coefficients, nor the three-block hybrid/correction's 450/52 coefficients, is a direct same-frame ADD. The exact native checker validates 120 candidate rank-1 child recipes to bring these role frames to frame 1. Charging one common-frame pass lowers the 3/5/9/14-block sensitivities to 0.002797088144, 0.006698357356, 0.013825363860 and 0.021482998123, respectively.

These are optimistic planning sensitivities, not a scalar tariff, admitted supplier, proved schedule or achieved κ. For the three-block prefix, pre-`B` placement avoids the 120 post-`B` frame joins; the one-pass post-`B` profile excludes restoration and separate dirty-baseline execution. Adapter-expanded endpoint semantics, changed-cut installation, frame-value lifetimes, dirty-baseline availability, any duplicated `B` execution and the full bit-side invoice remain unproved. The selected κ remains `0.001672660197076918`; no frontier update or universal frame-join obstruction is claimed.

## Task and overlap

Task card `coverage-law-change`, priority revision 6; scope refined to the source-bound P112 consumer and a comparison of pre-`B` placement with exact post-`B` retiming under selected native frame labels. Package base: `b1ef0a5585418590320806c967383584c645132b`. Submission-refresh canonical `main`: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`; selected-result SHA-256: `bb2eaa58647b353f88d0aec2eafb9d30df1be53589231b23e12ceef3e4bad129`.

Adjacent [PR #3344](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3344) screens larger-child and multiple-unpaid budgets; [PR #3566](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3566) binds the P112 decoder to selected ports; [PR #3567](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3567) screens a one-sided tetrad alphabet. This follow-up adds a source-bound inverse-transpose reader and exact native frame-join audit; it makes no general novelty claim. The cached overlap scan covers 394 PRs and 2,319 discussions as of 2026-10-18 03:15 UTC, but refresh failed, so this is not a novelty certificate.

## Validation

Replayed with CPython 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 -B research/p112-tetrad-cut-consumer/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-tetrad-cut-consumer --check-only
git diff --check
```

The verifier pins the selected archive, program, native lift and exact Clifford child recipes. It checks the 176 native cut coefficients and chronology, reconstructs the fourteen tetrads, verifies the hybrid identities and dirty correction, audits pre-`B` common-frame labels, expands the canonical `B` map, checks inverse-transpose identities and prefix sensitivities, audits post-`B` role-frame labels, and exactly checks the 120 candidate rank-1 joins. It claims no changed native schedule, adapter-expanded implementation, physical scalar tariff, supplier admission or complete outer invoice.

## Credit

The P112 geometry, selected-port bijection, gauge44 word, native-lift recipes and bit-side price engine retain their predecessor attribution. This follow-up adds the hybrid dirty-state correction, exact canonical post-`B` readout maps, and native frame-join sensitivities. Prepared by Gonzalo Mier with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Can the three-block hybrid and dirty correction be installed at the native pre-`B` frame-0 cut while retaining the separate dirty baseline? Bind one tetrad through adapters, `A`, the cut, `B`, cleanup and endpoint; track both streams and frame-value lifetimes, then price the added scalar operations.
2. Can a concrete complex supplier, exact scalar tariff and admitted bit-side supplier keep the complete joint target above `0.003`? Replace the rank-72 and rank-1-incidence assumptions with a complete source-bound invoice, including restoration and the separate dirty-baseline stream.
